overview: Kerma was a Nubian royal center on the Middle Nile. Its kingdom must be distinguished from the earlier Pre-Kerma settlement and from later Napatan and Meroitic Kush.

items.text: Residents combined livestock keeping and cultivation with fishing and hunting. Houses included courtyards with cooking and storage areas.
Exchange connected Kerma with Egypt, the Red Sea and African interiors through cattle, ivory, gold, hides and other goods.
The capital had successive defensive walls and ditches. A religious quarter included the Deffufa temple, chapels, workshops and stores.
A palace and a large circular structure interpreted as an audience hall occupied the political quarter.
The excavation mission places Egyptian destruction of the capital around 1450 BCE. Occupation and transition phases overlap conventional round dates for the kingdom.
